macro_regime: energy supply shock + sanctions escalation squeezing EM importers; EM tech momentum rolling over after outsized YTD run
thesis_summary: Short EM vs. global benchmark. The Hormuz closure (since Mar 2026) has Brent up ~21% y/y at ~$77 and tightening secondary sanctions on Russian/Iranian barrels raise the terms-of-trade tax on the big EM importers (China, India, Turkey, CEE) that dominate EEM, while the AI/semis complex that carried EEM +17% YTD is now the source of its underperformance (EEM/ACWI -6.1% over 3m). Consensus (GS, BlackRock weekly) remains constructive EM, leaving positioning a headwind if the ratio's downtrend extends toward the 52-week low.
thesis_detail: Prices verified this session, Aug 7 2026 close: EEM 65.64, ACWI 161.43, EFA 108.55, SPY 773.12. EEM/ACWI ratio 0.4066, 50th percentile of its 52-week range (hi 0.4519 / lo 0.3706); 1m -4.4%, 3m -6.1%, YTD +2.9% — i.e., all of EM's relative gains have been given back since May. Fundamental driver stack is now one-sided against EM beta: (1) Energy — crude ~$77/bbl, +20.7% y/y (TradingEconomics, Aug 7), with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed since March (House of Commons Library brief, Aug 7); EEM's heavyweight economies are net energy importers, so the shock is a direct terms-of-trade and inflation hit. (2) Sanctions — US Senate voted 86-12 on Jul 28 to advance the Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act; Rosneft/Lukoil already designated; Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy infrastructure are removing export capacity (Steptoe, Aug 4). Escalation path points to secondary-sanctions risk on India/China buyers — directly negative for two of EEM's three largest country weights. (3) Momentum/positioning — 'EM loses momentum as AI volatility, oil prices test investors' (Seeking Alpha, ~Aug 1); sell-side consensus still expects EM FX/equity resilience (GS AM, Aug 4), so the pain trade is further underperformance. CEEMEA-specific color: CEE disinflation is real (Czech CPI 1.5%, Hungary 1.7%, Poland 2.5% in June per national prints) but Polish CPI is set to re-accelerate to ~3.1% in July on fuel; NBP held at 3.75% for a fourth meeting, CNB is the region's hawk with ~2 hikes priced. CEE is a small EEM weight, so this proposal is a broad EM-underperformance expression driven by the energy/sanctions channel — the cleanest instrument the mandate allows. Acknowledged weakness: the oil shock is five months old and partly priced; the trade needs the second derivative (sanctions enforcement, AI-complex derating) to keep working.

base_case: Oil holds $75-90 with Hormuz constrained, sanctions enforcement tightens incrementally, and the AI/semis complex consolidates its YTD gain; EM importers' terms-of-trade drag persists and EEM/ACWI grinds toward 0.376 over 1-3 months.
bull_case: Escalation leg: final passage and aggressive enforcement of the Graham act with secondary sanctions on Indian/Chinese buyers, or renewed Hormuz disruption pushing crude >$100; EM capital flight accelerates and the ratio overshoots toward/below the 52w low of 0.3706 — trade outperforms target.
bear_case: Invalidation: Iran de-escalation reopens Hormuz and crude breaks below $70, or a durable Ukraine ceasefire triggers sanctions-relief repricing; EM risk-on squeeze with consensus positioning amplifying the move — ratio recovers above 0.4245 and the thesis of persistent EM underperformance is wrong. Stop hit.
key_risks: Instrument mismatch: EEM is ~75% Asia; the CEEMEA energy/sanctions view transmits mainly through China/India import costs and global risk premium, not directly
Oil shock is five months old and partially priced; de-escalation unwinds it fast against a crowded-consensus long-EM backdrop (squeeze risk cuts both ways)
Fed path: a dovish surprise weakens the dollar and historically lifts EM beta regardless of the oil drag
Chasing risk: ratio already -6% over 3m; entry at the 50th percentile is mid-range, not stretched
